newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Democrats release Senate fundraising subpoena.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Democrats release Senate fundraising subpoena.

text.p: The Senate committee investigating campaign fund raising asked the Democratic National Committee for documents related to communications with 117 individuals and groups, according to a subpoena released on Wednesday.
The DNC released a copy of the subpoena, which was issued in the spring, to bolster its complaint that the congressional request for information was too broad.
The Senate Governmental Affairs Committee planned to start four weeks of hearings on campaign financing next week.
Congress and the Justice Department were investigating allegations that foreign countries may have sought to influence the 1996 presidential and congressional elections with campaign contributions.

At the top of the list, the subpoena sought communications between the DNC and the Lippo Group, an Indonesia-based financial conglomerate, and James Riady, one of its high officials. There were several requests for information connected to former Democratic fund-raiser John Huang, including his appointment books, telephone calls and electronic mail.
The Lippo Group, Riady and Huang, who had worked for the Lippo Group, were under investigation by U.S. officials looking into foreign influence-peddling and illegal donations.
The list also included U.S. labour organisations such as the AFL-CIO and the International Brotherhood of Teamsters.
The subpoena also sought documents of communications between the DNC and the United States Export-Import Bank, the Clinton Birthplace Foundation and the Cheyenne-Arapaho Indians of Oklahoma.
Guest lists for events which President Clinton, first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton or Vice President Al Gore were scheduled to attend from 1995 onward also were sought.
